title: Synth Templates — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Synth Templates' rich face, its first round at Sketch tier, a proposal. Beside the card's three parts I lay the house bass's own sheet and its reference render as the workshop made them, and the site that plays it; under the split I put one piece that plays the card on the project's own voice and asks the project's own meters, then an ear, whether the knobs the card calls taste keep the sound and the ones it calls essential lose it. I grow when Loudon's ear answers the blind trials and when the card or the comparison page changes. I never hold the entry's words.
grain: Coarse, and the page's own: the body is one section (the H1's) holding the three card parts as bold paragraphs, then Neighbours and Forward Vectors with no pieces. Everything here is in that one section, so it is approved all or nothing. No ### inside, so no hidden sub-sections.
whose_numbers: This card's and this project's: cards/house-bass.yaml (card 0.2) through workshop/vocabulary.yaml draft 0.6 as on disk, played by workshop/site/voice.js and measured by workshop/site/compare.js (both generated by build-site.py, inlined byte for byte, sha256 c855c2beb861 and 020c902aac4b at main 5bc2c13a). Not the VCV knob numbers in pdl/house-bass.pdl, and not Generative Audio Devices' house_bass.pdl (a saw, the card's lineage).
not_verified: No agent can hear a mix: nothing here was listened to, and the blind trials have no answers yet. Verified headless (Chromium, 48 kHz, compressor on) by 'Synth Templates — rich — check.mjs': the inlined voice, analyser, card and vocabulary equal the workshop's; the baked table reproduces; the repeat check holds; the loudness match lands within 0.02 dB with no peak past -0.72 dBFS; the chance figures; the playDemo count. Not checked: how the piece sounds in Safari or Firefox, the live face's public build, and whether a 1 % brightness grain is a fair tolerance (the A/B clears it on the bar by 0.4 %).

offers.what: Not a text edit; for the house-bass card (workshop/cards/house-bass.yaml). The card pins the filter envelope's decay as essential (short) and lists it again as taste (short – medium), and the sheet prints both. On the card's own bar the far end of that taste range and the card's A/B are nearly the same sound: decay to medium measures level -17.4 dBFS, brightness 155 Hz, rise 25 ms, tail 150 ms; sustain to full measures -17.4, 157 Hz, 25 ms, 150 ms. A 0.575 s decay never finishes inside a 121 ms note. Held 0.8 s they part (100 Hz against 158 Hz). Either the decay comes off one list, or the taste range stops short of medium, or the split is stated for held notes. Loudon's ear on the blind trials (both moves are in them) decides which.

Not a text edit; for the house-bass card's render spec and Plan move 4. The numbers hold: on the bar the A/B moves brightness 102.7 → 157.4 Hz, held 68.8 → 157.6 Hz. The A/B itself is plain on the bar, since at sustain full the filter never decays. What the bar cannot show is the difference between the A/B and the taste end of the filter decay: decay medium (0.575 s) never finishes inside a 121 ms note, so it reads 155.2 Hz on the bar against the A/B's 157.4, and only parts from it on a held note (100.2 against 157.6). A reference render that ends on one held note would let a learner hear why decay short is pinned.

Not a text edit; for build-site.py's readPattern (it writes site/voice.js). Given this card's pattern, 'offbeat eighths, one bar: rest C2 rest C2 rest C2 rest C2, each a 16th long', Play the default schedules eight notes 60 ms long on the off-sixteenths; the card writes four notes 121 ms long on the off-eighths. The unit regex matches '16th' before 'eighth', and 'a 16th long' then halves the gate. renders/house-bass.png shows the eight. The workshop README's line that playDemo does not read pattern is also out of date. Checked by the check script, which counts the voice's own noteOn calls.

Not a text edit; for Plan move 5, the comparison page (compare.js readings, buildReport). On the house bass its verdict cannot be trusted as a measure of lost. It reads the untouched held note's wave as 'triangle' and its resonance as 'high' (the card says square, moderate). Oscillator 1 swapped for noise reads 'triangle' from the sub under it, and on the card's bar the page calls that noise sound a match on 4 of 8 noise seeds. The reading meant for the card's A/B, the filter's sustain, calls the A/B a match on both clips ('falls 1.6 oct' against '1.2' on the bar, '1.7' against '0.6' held: low against half, adjacent). The amp-sustain reading sits on its own thresholds (crest 12.4 dB on the bar against 12, 7.3 held against 8), so taste moves flip it. Across 16 moves it agrees with the card's split on 8 (bar) and 10 (held). The four sidecar numbers do no better (9 and 10): they measure how far a knob moves the sound, not which way matters. The challenger re-ran it on the site's own playDemo pattern and found it worse there: nothing flags the A/B, noise passes as a match on 2 of 8 seeds, agreement 8 of 16.

A question for Loudon, for the card and the page: the card pins square as essential ('change one and it stops being a house bass'), and the page's own first paragraph says it too ('House Bass: mono, square, percussive filter envelope'), while the card's lineage line, Generative Audio Devices' house_bass.pdl, is a saw (OSC:SAW -> FILT:IN), the file the page calls the first house-bass recipe. The saw move is in the blind trials: if his ear calls it still house bass, the essential may be 'a rich wave, filtered' (the card's own concept line) rather than square.

For Loudon: the page and its card disagree on resonance. The page's second paragraph lists 'resonance amount' among the taste settings ('The taste settings are what a player moves: cutoff, resonance amount, release length'); the card pins filter 1 resonance moderate as essential (cards/house-bass.yaml, essentials: 'the vowel in the "ooh"') and lists no resonance in taste. The piece follows the card and scores both resonance moves essential, one in the blind trials. Either the page's example list drops resonance amount, or the card moves it to taste. The meters cannot settle it: on the bar meter A calls moderate → none kept and moderate → high lost, meter B the reverse.

pieces.title: House bass · signal-flow sheet, card 0.2
pieces.caption: **The sheet the paragraph describes, as the generator draws it.** Oscillator and sub into the mixer, the 24 dB low-pass, the amplifier; the two envelopes beneath, each block carrying its glyph. Essentials in ink, taste in amber. Read the filter envelope: decay appears twice, short in ink and short – medium in amber. That one parameter is on both lists, and the piece below finds it is where the split is thinnest. Gathered as drawn, not redrawn.

pieces.title: House bass · reference render spectrogram
pieces.caption: **The reference render, from the project's own voice.** Its sidecar reads peak -3.65 dBFS, RMS -16.3, centroid 147 Hz, rise 25 ms, tail 145 ms (renders/features.json). It shows eight notes where the card writes four: the site's pattern reader takes 'each a 16th long' as sixteenths and halves the gate (see the offers). The WAV itself is ignored by git and not on the public face.

pieces.title: Which knobs are which · the house bass split, two meters and an ear
pieces.caption: **Tests the split.** It walks up: the house bass untouched; one taste knob alone (cutoff, dark to mid); one essential alone (the filter's sustain, the card's A/B); then every knob the voice models moved and judged by two meters with rules written first, on the card's bar and on a held note: meter A is this piece's rule over the project's four sidecar numbers (not a project meter; its taste misses happen by construction), meter B the project's own comparison verdict; then twelve blind trials, loudness-matched, scored on both arms. Where the page and the card disagree (resonance: taste on the page, essential on the card), the piece follows the card and says so. Measured: neither meter sees the split whole (9, 8, 10 and 10 of 16), the comparison page fails its own noise control on the bar, and on the card's bar the taste end of the filter decay sounds almost like the A/B. These are findings about the meters and the card, not a verdict on the page: which knobs are structural is a teaching rule, and the trials put it to the ear. Re-checked by 'Synth Templates — rich — check.mjs'.

verdicts.why: The sheet the paragraph describes, gathered as drawn; its caption's 'decay on both lists' is true (house-bass.tex:124: decay short in ink, short – medium in amber).
Captioned honestly: its sidecar numbers match renders/features.json (−3.65 / −16.33 dBFS, 147 Hz, 25 ms, 145 ms) and its eight notes are offer 3's readPattern reading, confirmed.

verdicts.why: A real test that walks up and whose blind trials hold (no leak, matched, both arms, 7/64 right). Fix: the page calls resonance amount taste and the piece scores it essential unnamed; step 3's 'little room' mechanism is wrong (sustain full means no decay; bar 102.7 → 157.4 Hz); meter A is the maker's rule on the project's features, not the project's meter. See the challenge record.

left_out: The record's gathered list also named workshop/site/index.html and workshop/picker.html. The site was tried and left out: it loads its sheets through site/sheets, a symlink to ../cards, which the piece origin does not serve, so on the face every card page would show a broken sheet (conform: file-missing). The picker is the Completeness Tracker for Plan move 2, not anything the opening section says. The record's second made piece, a signal-flow sheet in the house style, is the card's own sheet, gathered, not redrawn.
